newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ousted Sierra Leone leader says he still president.
newsitem.headline: Ousted Sierra Leone leader says he still president.

text.p: Sierra Leone's ousted leader Ahmad Tejan Kabbah said from exile on Tuesday he was still the president despite the declared takeover of power by soldiers.

Kabbah, who fled to neighbouring Guinea as Sunday's coup unfolded, was asked in a BBC Africa Service radio interview whether he would try to take back his job, now claimed by coup leader Major Johnny Paul Koromah.
"It is not a question of taking back my job. I am the president of Sierra Leone," Kabbah said in the interview monitored in Abidjan.
"Somebody is just masquerading as president," he said.
"I am sad and angry because I am a Sierra Leonean and I see and I hear and I know that a group of hooligans are destroying my country," Kabbah added.

Residents of the capital said the coup by lower-ranking soldiers did not appear to have the full backing of the army. Koromah was freed from Freetown's maximum security prison where he was detained on charges of plotting against Kabbah.
The coup forces stormed the prison and distributed arms to hundreds of inmates who joined their cause.

Kabbah said his one regret was to have rejected the advice of his aides for a summary trial of Koromah, "which could have led to execution". Kabbah, a lawyer, said he asked for the trial to follow due process.
The United States called for restoration of Kabbah who was elected little more than a year ago. The United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity have also condemned the coup.
